verdict.rationale: RunAnywhere's core design keeps data on-device ('Private by default. Offline by design.'; prompts/audio/images stay on the phone) and explicit control over when any request leaves the machine, which by construction prevents data from reaching a server that could train on it — corroborated by a community reply confirming 'no data is collected' for local use. Hosted/cloud execution (Wally) is opt-in and explicit rather than silent, though there's no explicit documented training-data policy for the cloud tier. Missing for 10: an explicit stated no-training-on-user-data policy for the hosted/cloud path, and independent audit confirming no telemetry.
